title: Morning Edition
dek: A UN mission's uncertain future, contested maritime incidents, a Polish judicial crisis, and a quieter village Samhain.

lead_story.headline: Rival UN resolutions fail, leaving Western Sahara peacekeeping mandate to expire
lead_story.summary: Russia vetoed a US proposal that would have favored Moroccan sovereignty and changed the UN mission in Western Sahara. A Russian proposal to extend the existing mandate then failed to win enough votes. The 35-year-old MINURSO mission's mandate expires October 31, with the territory's political status still unresolved.
lead_story.why_it_matters: A monitoring mission may end without a replacement agreement. Morocco, the Polisario Front and outside powers disagree over whether autonomy under Moroccan sovereignty or a vote on independence should guide the settlement.

items.headline: Iran claims four tankers hit mines; maritime monitors confirm separate incidents
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said four tankers struck mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on October 30. Reuters and AP could not independently verify that tally or identify all four ships. Oman reported evacuating 25 crew from a damaged tanker, while UK maritime monitors recorded projectile strikes whose relationship to Iran's claims is unclear.
items.why_it_matters: The difference between a belligerent's claims and independently documented shipping incidents matters in a waterway central to global energy trade.

items.headline: Poland's constitutional court standoff brings president back from flight to Senegal
items.summary: A judge announced the suspension of Poland's Constitutional Tribunal chief on October 30 amid a long-running dispute over appointments. Police secured the court as protesters gathered. President Karol Nawrocki turned his plane around, while government and opposition figures offered sharply different accounts of the legality of the intervention.
items.why_it_matters: A contest over who may lawfully lead the court tests the credibility of attempts to repair judicial independence without reproducing political control.

items.headline: Conflicting reports of deadly drone strikes on Ethiopian displacement camp
items.summary: Independent reporting describes drone strikes on the Jari 2 camp in Ethiopia's Amhara region on October 29. Reuters reported at least 15 deaths from rescue sources; Anadolu reported at least 16 and Ethiopian outlet Borkena cited local estimates ranging higher. Neither the responsible force nor a definitive toll has been independently established.
items.why_it_matters: Displaced families have again been exposed to violence, while inconsistent casualty accounts and uncertain attribution demand careful verification rather than premature certainty.

items.headline: Recent miss: Oleshky evacuation convoys begin under a rare local truce
items.summary: Buses began taking civilians out of Russian-occupied Oleshky on October 30 under a six-day localized pause. Ukrainian and Russian ombuds officials participated; residents were offered choices to leave for either side or stay with replenished aid. Numbers evacuated and whether the model can be repeated remain unsettled.
items.why_it_matters: A limited, observable humanitarian opening is different from a general ceasefire, but may show what narrowly negotiated civilian protections can achieve.
items.source: Associated Press — Hanna Arhirova, Kherson field reporting

items.headline: Older catch-up: prime assembly broadens the range of possible genome edits
items.summary: A September 16 Nature paper describes 'prime assembly,' a CRISPR-guided method for integrating larger DNA fragments and making rearrangements in human cells. The team demonstrated activity in primary human cells and non-dividing cells; this is laboratory method development, not a clinical treatment.
items.why_it_matters: The technique addresses a practical limitation of gene editing: changing more than a few DNA letters without relying on conventional double-strand-break approaches.

items.headline: To decipher burned Roman scrolls, researchers made and burned new ones
items.summary: Researchers reproduced charred papyrus and tested lead-containing inks with X-ray imaging. A September PLOS One study found that even small amounts of lead made letters much easier to detect in their model scrolls. Whether surviving Herculaneum scrolls contain enough leaded ink is still unknown.
items.why_it_matters: An inventive experiment may help scholars decide which fragile ancient texts can be scanned without opening them.

items.headline: A village in León revives Samhain with chestnuts, storytelling and folk dance
items.summary: Rioscuro de Laciana, in Spain's León province, has scheduled an October 31 Samhain gathering with a walk through the village, children's activities, a shared intergenerational 'calecho,' roasted chestnuts and traditional dance. Local reporting presents it as a community celebration of seasonal memory.
items.why_it_matters: A small village's autumn calendar offers a view of ordinary cultural life beyond the scale of national headlines.

items.headline: If a species can be recreated, what exactly has been saved?
items.summary: Historian Sadiah Qureshi argues that frozen genomes and engineered substitutes should not be mistaken for preserving a living species, its learned behavior and ecological relationships. Her essay asks whether promises of de-extinction could weaken our obligations to protect existing habitats and animals.
items.why_it_matters: The question changes how conservation success is defined: genetic similarity, ecological function and a living way of being are not interchangeable.

worth_your_time.headline: A scientist's case for optimism begins with uncertainty, not certainty
worth_your_time.summary: In Undark, biologist C. Brandon Ogbunu reviews Stuart Firestein's It Could Be Otherwise, a book arguing that scientific uncertainty and historical contingency are reasons to remain curious, not reasons to despair. The review also distinguishes that intellectual optimism from empty assurances that progress is inevitable.
worth_your_time.why_it_matters: A reflective account of how science advances through incomplete knowledge offers a counterweight to both technological triumphalism and fatalism.

editorial_review.section_uniqueness_check: pass — ten unique canonical story URLs across lead, three other Front Page items, two catch-up selections, discovery, Human Scale, Ideas and one distinct Long Read; no duplicated source piece.
editorial_review.human_scale_stakes_check: pass — Rioscuro's Samhain walk, chestnuts, intergenerational storytelling and dance are low-stakes village culture; not a hardship, service-access or safety-crisis item.
editorial_review.triangulation_check: pass with disclosed limits — Western Sahara: independent AP and Reuters UN-vote reporting plus Morocco-based French Hespress for the royal position; competing autonomy and self-determination positions are attributed. Hormuz: Reuters and AP with Omani evacuation and UKMTO maritime observations; the Iranian four-tanker count and mine mechanism are unverified. Poland: original Polish Rzeczpospolita court coverage, Notes from Poland and independent AP/Reuters; legality remains contested. Ethiopia: Ethiopian-source Borkena and Addis Standard witness material reported by Anadolu, plus Reuters' separate rescue interviews and AFP witnesses; counts range at least 14–24 and perpetrator is unproven. Oleshky: AP field reporting, Ukrainian ombuds and separate Russian-side accounts; evacuation totals remain uncertain. Laboratory research is primary peer-reviewed evidence; essays and review are argument interpretation.
editorial_review.contextualization_check: pass — nine URL-keyed substantive Continue Reading treatments add verified background, competing accounts, limitations, wider stakes and next signals. The Ideas reader reconstructs question, thesis, premises, an example, strong objection and implications; the book-review reader separates Firestein's thesis from Ogbunu's assessment. Human Scale intentionally remains concise.

editorial_review.difference_from_recent: Moves from Iranian procurement, Korean launches, Colombian fiscal legislation and port labor actions to a Western Sahara UN mandate failure, newly reported Hormuz incidents, Poland's court standoff and Ethiopia's disputed camp attack.
notes_for_next_edition: Check whether MINURSO actually winds down and what protection arrangements remain.
Seek independent vessel identities and maritime incident logs before treating Iran's four-tanker tally as verified.
Track Poland's planned November 3 judicial assembly and any independent legal ruling.
Reconcile Jari 2 casualty reports and verify attribution only with independent evidence.
Check Oleshky evacuation counts and completion before the localized pause ends.
